editorial:
You follow a pizza delivery driver named Marco who shows up to a creepy old house on a Friday night and never makes it back to his car. What starts as a normal delivery turns into a wild weekend where his friends, family, and even the cops start seeing weird things around town. The movie has a dark but playful vibe, mixing real sadness with strange, funny moments that keep you guessing. It feels like a late-night story a friend would tell you, and that makes it easy to sink into.

The acting is strong, especially the lead who makes you care about Marco even after he is gone. The pacing moves fast, with short scenes that never drag, though some side plots feel a bit rushed. The music and lighting give it a moody look without being too heavy. If you like character-driven drama with a mystery twist, this is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you learn Marco did not just die by accident. The creepy house owner had been luring delivery drivers for years. Marco's ghost starts leaving clues, like pizza boxes with notes, that lead his sister to the basement. There she finds proof of the crimes. The owner tries to run but is caught by police. Marco's spirit finally rests, and his sister delivers one last pizza in his honor.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven drama with a mystery twist
